findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to application logs
findings.body: Every call to `recordIssuedToken` passes the complete authentication token to the console-backed audit function. In environments that retain or forward stdout, anyone with log access can replay still-valid credentials and impersonate affected users. Log non-sensitive issuance metadata instead.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body: When `returnUrl` originates from login state or a query parameter, values such as an external HTTPS URL or dangerous URL scheme are passed directly to `location.assign`. This enables trusted login links to redirect authenticated users to attacker-controlled content. Accept only validated same-origin paths or an explicit allowlist.

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to the console-backed audit logger
findings.body:
Every call records the complete bearer token through `console.log`. In production environments where console output is retained or accessible to operators/services, anyone reading those logs can replay still-valid tokens and take over affected sessions.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict login return URLs before navigating
findings.body:
Any caller-provided value, such as `https://evil.example/phish`, now redirects users away from the application after login. If `returnUrl` comes from a query parameter or authentication state, attackers can create trusted login links that end on an attacker-controlled site; dangerous URL schemes may also be accepted by the browser.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to approved same-origin paths
findings.body:
When `returnUrl` comes from login query/form state, an attacker can supply an external or dangerous-scheme URL and redirect an authenticated victim to attacker-controlled content. The previous fixed destination did not cross this trust boundary.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Stop writing issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body:
Every call with a live bearer/session token writes the credential verbatim to the console. In deployments that retain or forward stdout, anyone with log access can recover tokens and impersonate users until expiration.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
